## December 2024: envoys, canals and the funding fight

In December 2024, President-elect Trump named television producer [[mark-burnett|Mark Burnett]] — the man behind [[the-apprentice|The Apprentice]] — as special envoy to the United Kingdom, saying Burnett brought "a unique blend of diplomatic acumen and international recognition to this important role."[{n}] The selection was described as continuing his trend of staffing the incoming administration with figures from television or politics, alongside defense secretary pick [[pete-hegseth|Pete Hegseth]] and [[mehmet-oz|Mehmet Oz]].[{n}]

The same weekend, Trump threatened to demand the return of the [[panama-canal|Panama Canal]] if [[panama|Panama]] did not lower its transit fees, writing on Truth Social that "this complete 'rip-off' of our Country will immediately stop" and calling President [[jimmy-carter|Jimmy Carter]]'s 1979 treaty a foolish giveaway made "for One Dollar."[{n}] Badlands writer [[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] framed these moves as narrative "deployments" derived from The Art of the Deal and Sun Tzu's Art of War, noting that Trump's deal-making was on display across borders and oceans before he had even taken office — with [[justin-trudeau|Justin Trudeau]] in a Trump-provoked death spiral to the north and [[claudia-sheinbaum|Claudia Sheinbaum]] pressed to take the fight to the cartels to the south.[{n}]

Domestically, Trump's eleventh-hour intervention in the government funding fight — backed by [[elon-musk|Elon Musk]] — led Speaker [[mike-johnson|Mike Johnson]] to trash his initial deal with Democrats and brought the country to the brink of a holiday shutdown, with The Hill describing House Republicans as governed by an effort to appease "an audience of one."[{n}] His insistence that any package include a debt-ceiling hike infuriated House conservatives, and Rep. Bob Good, former head of the [[house-freedom-caucus|House Freedom Caucus]], said "trying to raise the debt limit was a mistake."[{n}]
